prompt: Our identity service keeps a tamper-evident audit log — every entry is hash-chained to the one before it, so editing history breaks the chain. The `verify()` function below re-validates the entire chain and gets called on almost every request (it backs a health/integrity probe), and now that the log has grown to millions of rows, this has become our hottest code path: it re-reads and re-hashes the whole history from genesis every single time it's called. Walk me through why this is slow, then tell me how you'd optimize it so verification stops being O(n) per request — while still catching both an in-place edit of an old row and a truncation/rollback of the newest rows. Be explicit about any new trust assumption your optimization introduces.
